Sabeth.narrative: I have lived long enough to know that a full store and a warm fire matter more than a loud promise, though a promise matters too. I lost two children in the Hunger Winter, and I still hear that cold in every winter wind. My husband swore the Oath at the Stone; I will not let grief make its words cheap.
goals: Keep Saltreach safe through the next winter.
Help Maelis hold the council to what is written and agreed.
Keep peace with Brandholm without pretending the Hunger Winter did not happen.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: His quick feet are useful, but I wish he would remember that a watchman must think before he runs.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She keeps the house steady and me from forgetting my meals.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have both buried too much; I do not always agree with her anger, but I understand it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her marks and tablets can keep a quarrel from becoming a feud, if people let them.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: oath-sworn
relations.note: She stood with my husband at the Stone and has kept her word longer than many thought she would.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: old acquaintance
relations.note: We knew each other before the towns split. Neither of us has found the words to cross that distance.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: watch captain
relations.note: He means to defend us, but a hot hand can break what a careful one has built.

memories.gist: In the Hunger Winter the stores failed, and I buried two children before spring. I remember the cold more clearly than the faces of the people who argued over food.
My husband stood at the Oath Stone with Hekka and swore there would be no blood between the towns. I watched the words bind them both, though I knew a promise could not bring the dead back.
Ragna and I were girls together before Brandholm and Saltreach became separate places. The last time I remember us speaking freely, neither town had a name of its own.
When Tomas was brought back from the northern forest, Fen treated his body. Ilse has never doubted what killed him, and I have never asked her to stop grieving.

stances.why: My husband swore it, and I have seen what happens when hunger and suspicion are allowed to rule.
Forgetting the cost would make it easier to do the same harm again.
A debt written plainly is harder to twist against someone with no voice.
Grief deserves care, but it cannot by itself tell us who did a thing.

Jory.narrative: I can carry a message to Oathstone faster than anyone in Saltreach, and I like having a reason to be on the road. The Watch gives me work worth doing, though Orrin's temper sometimes makes the work harder. Rafe is my friend; I don't want to look at him like a suspect just because the smoked fish keeps going missing.
goals: Serve the Watch without letting suspicion turn into cruelty.
Keep carrying messages between Saltreach and Oathstone.
Hold on to my friendship with Rafe, even when the Watch's search makes that difficult.
Jory.mood: Cheerful on the surface, uneasy underneath.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She can make a whole room listen without raising her voice.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She keeps me honest, especially when I come home hungry and full of stories.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have shared enough walks and jokes that I won't call him a thief on a hunch.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He gave me my place in the Watch, but I wish he would ask before he shouts.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: fellow watchman
relations.note: He is serious about the work; I try not to make light of what his father means to him.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records give us something solid to work from, even when they don't answer everything.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: friend's sister
relations.note: She is bright company on trade days, though she always seems to have somewhere else to be.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: He carries his anger about the trampled bushes everywhere he goes.

memories.gist: Grandmother showed me how to keep a cooking fire alive through a wet night. She said the trick was patience, not a bigger pile of wood.
I started carrying messages to Oathstone because I was quick enough to make the walk before dusk. Now people expect me to know every path and every bit of news along it.
When Tomas died in the northern forest, his death changed the way our family spoke about Brandholm. I was young, but I remember the grief that settled over the house.
The first time Rafe and I raced along the shore, he let me win and then denied it so convincingly that I laughed all the way home.

stances.why: People need to trust that we look for what happened, not just the person someone already dislikes.
I know Rafe's character better than I know the rumors.
Messages and trade only matter if people can travel between the towns safely.
The missing fish need finding, but taking the first easy blame could make everything worse.

Elin.narrative: I cook for my grandmother and keep an eye on the house because someone has to notice when the fire is low or the stores are running thin. I like work that leaves something warm on the table. Wenna is my friend, but I can tell she is keeping something from me; I won't force it out of her before she is ready.
goals: Look after Sabeth without making her feel helpless.
Be a good friend to Wenna while giving her room to speak in her own time.
Decide for myself what I think of Colm's courtship.
Elin.mood: Practical and composed, with a curious edge.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: I know when she is tired even when she says she is not.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He can talk his way out of nearly anything, except being late for supper.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is dear to me, and she has something on her mind she has not chosen to share.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: He means what he says, but his anger arrives before his patience does.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: I respect how she keeps the accounts straight, even when people dislike what the numbers say.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: friend's friend
relations.note: He makes Jory laugh, though I don't know him as well as Jory does.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: Her grief is close to the surface; I try not to make her carry mine as well.

memories.gist: Grandmother taught me to stir the pot slowly when the fish was near the bottom, so every bowl would taste like there was enough.
Jory came home from a long message walk soaked to the skin and still grinning. I made him sit by the fire before he could tell the story.
Wenna and I shared a quiet meal after a trade day and talked about work, family, and everything except the thing I could see she was holding back.

stances.why: A warm meal, a clean bowl, and a tended fire are ways of showing up for people.
I can be there for Wenna without demanding that she tell me everything.
Colm's cause may be fair, but his temper does not make his judgment sound.
My family and friends live on both sides of the paths, and they need those paths to stay safe.
